clue.text: As old leaders of poverty hit and repressively armed oil nation in crisis

annotationWithheld.why: As old leaders of poverty hit and repressively armed oil nation in crisis: the first letters of 'poverty ... crisis' spell the answer, but 'leaders' must be both the acrostic indicator and part of the definition 'As old leaders'
annotationWithheld.clue: As old leaders of poverty hit and repressively armed oil nation in crisis

clue.text: Sets up loan to exchange (set up around completion of transaction)

indicators.note: around means the swap word encloses the final letter of transaction
in a down clue, set up means the word is raised so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to exchange is to swap

indicators.note: the completion of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style gloss of pawning: arranging a loan by handing over goods, the swap being set up around finishing the deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts N, the last letter of transaction, into SWAP to give SWANP; 'set up' then turns that upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To pawn something is to raise a loan by pledging it as security, so a pawnbroker deal is a loan set up that way.

clue.text: Two things Charles is but Camilla isn't, in speech to deliver abroad?

indicators.note: in speech means the words are to be heard spoken rather than read as spelt

parts.words: Two things Charles is but Camilla isn't
parts.note: Charles was heir to the throne and is male; his wife Camilla is neither

explanation.surface: A royal riddle about what Prince Charles is and the Duchess of Cornwall is not.
explanation.walkthrough: Written when Charles was Prince of Wales: he was HEIR and he is MALE; said together they give the postal service word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending letters by plane is the usual way to dispatch post overseas, so the verb sense means to send abroad.

clue.text: Contract for removal: right and good to make a home

indicators.note: for removal says the named letters are taken away from the shortened word

parts.note: to contract a text is to shorten it, to abridge it

explanation.surface: A removals firm agrees terms, the contract being right and good, so a family can settle in.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide somewhere is an old word for to dwell or live there, to make one's home.

clue.text: Overnight shift after close match

indicators.note: after puts the word for match behind the word for close

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near or close
a tie is a match or fixture, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: Working a night shift after a close-fought match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like a work rota, but it is the old word for a woman's loose slip or dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a simple loose dress, and a nightdress is the version worn overnight in bed.

clue.text: See 15
Pine cleanser with immaculate finish

parts.note: a mop is a cleaning tool, here a cleanser

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A pine-scented cleaning product that leaves an immaculate finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' reads as the tree or the scent, but it is the verb to long or sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine and to brood both mean to languish listlessly in low spirits.

clue.text: Wine and cheese: uplifting with a little Gershwin

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplifting means the word is raised to read from bottom to top

parts.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese
Ira Gershwin, lyricist, was George Gershwin's younger brother, so 'a little Gershwin'

explanation.surface: A wine-and-cheese evening made uplifting by a bit of Gershwin music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns EDAM to MADE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a fortified wine from the Portuguese island of the same name.

clue.text: Getting together in positive mood, preparing for move

parts.note: packing is gathering or crowding together, as people pack a hall
up means cheerful, in good spirits

explanation.surface: Friends gather in a cheerful mood to get ready for a house move.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxing up belongings is what one does to get ready to change house.

clue.text: Getting together for party in new home, not saying by what means?

indicators.note: not saying means the sound of the question word is dropped from the party word

parts.note: a housewarming is the party thrown in a new home
by what means asks 'how', and the first part of house is said like 'how' plus S

explanation.surface: Friends gather for a party in a new home, but nobody says how they got there.
explanation.walkthrough: HOUSE is said 'how-s'; 'not saying' the 'how' sound leaves just S from it, so the removed HOU and E are the letters that carry that sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarming describes a crowd gathering or massing together, like bees round a hive.

clue.text: Denial set in code

indicators.note: set means the letters are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A refusal written in cipher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges the six letters of IN CODE.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase is an emphatic refusal, meaning 'no chance' or 'certainly not'.

clue.text: Eats cooked meal with man contracted to help in moving home?

definitions.text: contracted to help in moving home?

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are worked over into a new form

parts.note: tea is an evening meal in much of Britain
gent is short for gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: Someone eats a cooked meal with the man hired to help them move house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns EATS into ESTA. 'contracted' looks like a shortening signal but belongs to the definition: the hired agent is under contract.
explanation.definitionFit: A property seller's professional intermediary is engaged under contract to sell the house for them.

clue.text: Huge mistake in the event of being in spasm

indicators.note: being in says the next pieces sit inside the word for spasm

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary muscular spasm
to err is to make a mistake
if means in the event of

explanation.surface: A massive blunder made while someone was having a fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrific in its older sense means very great or tremendous in size or force.

clue.text: Decent homes for homeless wretches

indicators.note: being at home is 'in', so homeless means the word loses those letters

parts.note: villains are scoundrels or wretches

explanation.surface: Proper housing provided for wretched people living on the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'homeless' removes IN (at home) from VILLAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Villas are substantial detached houses, so decent homes in a residential sense.

clue.text: Moving home? Boatman is, in April or May

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: in places the setter's I inside the season word

parts.note: April and May are months of spring
Boatman is the setter, so he is I

explanation.surface: The setter claims to be inspired by moving house in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving home?' looks like a removals phrase, but only 'Moving' is the definition, in its stirring sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiring and moving both describe something that rouses the emotions.

clue.text: Floating algae fumes interrupt search and rescue: an additional problem

indicators.note: interrupt says the fumes word breaks into the other pieces

parts.note: a sum, especially an addition, is an arithmetic problem
fumes are gas

explanation.surface: Seaweed fumes get in the way of a search-and-rescue team, adding one more problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupt' sends the fumes between the rescue abbreviation and the sum. The surface reads like a news report; the algae are the definition, not a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Sargassum is a genus of brown seaweed that drifts in mats, as in the Sargasso Sea.

clue.text: Commit to buying a home, if trade picks up?

parts.note: to exchange is to trade one thing for another
to contract an illness is to pick it up

explanation.surface: A homebuyer is willing to sign up for a house if business improves.
explanation.walkthrough: In English property sale law, the buyer becomes bound when both parties swap signed contracts; 'picks up' reads as an upturn in business but means catches.
explanation.definitionFit: In English conveyancing this step is the point at which a buyer becomes legally bound to purchase.

clue.text: I set core cryptic!

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of making a core of cryptic clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' both rearranges I SET CORE and says what the result means: obscure.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric means understood only by a few initiates, obscure or hidden in meaning.

clue.text: Having a blast in South London

definitions.meaning: sounding a horn or whistle loudly
a district of the London Borough of Wandsworth, south of the Thames

explanation.definitionFit: Blowing a horn is hooting; the same word names a south London district near Wandsworth.

clue.text: Without much travail, not prevented from moving home

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the next word goes around the rest

parts.note: can means able to, not prevented

indicators.note: much of the word travail is used, its outer T and final IL dropped

explanation.surface: A family moves home easily, nothing standing in their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but is the old sense outside; 'much' keeps the middle of travail, dropping its outer letters, and CAN wraps that.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravan is a home on wheels that can be towed from place to place.

clue.text: Don't turn in before end of Pilates exercise

definitions.note: singular in the clue, but the answer names a type of exercise in the plural

indicators.note: before puts the staying-up phrase ahead of the last letter

parts.note: to sit up is to stay up and not go to bed

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Advice to stay up late before finishing a Pilates workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn in' is going to bed. 'Pilates' looks like part of the definition but only gives its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: These abdominal moves, raising the torso from lying, are a standard gym workout.

clue.text: No stamp duty to pay after exchanging?

indicators.note: changing means the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: the first two letters of exchanging, read as the word ex

explanation.surface: No stamp duty is due once contracts have been exchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'exchanging' into 'ex' and 'changing', the latter rearranging the rest. Stamp duty is a UK tax on property purchases, paid by the buyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Exempt from a levy means there is no tax payable, such as the stamp levy on property.

clue.text: Is around, evolved, or is gone

definitions.text: Is around, evolved, or is gone

indicators.note: evolved means the letters have developed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that lives on, develops or dies out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evolved' rearranges IS AROUND; the whole clue also describes an animal that was around, evolved and went extinct.
explanation.definitionFit: These prehistoric reptiles lived for ages, evolved into many forms and then became extinct.

clue.text: React badly about kiss for Cornish Tom

indicators.note: about means the jumbled word goes around the kiss
badly suggests the letters are jumbled into a poor order

parts.note: X is the symbol for a kiss

explanation.surface: Someone responds badly to a kiss from a Cornish man called Tom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' turns REACT into RECAT, and 'about' puts X inside it. 'Tom' looks like a man's name but is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cornish Rex is a curly-coated breed of domestic feline, and a tom is a male one.

clue.text: "One bad at heart without the head" — from speech in Ireland

indicators.note: without the head says the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a brogue is an Irish accent

explanation.surface: A quotation about a bad person, delivered in an Irish accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a scoundrel, a person whose nature is dishonest.

clue.text: See 10
Numbers of computers in temporary home

indicators.note: in says the computing word goes inside the lodgings word

parts.note: digs are lodgings, a temporary home
IT, information technology, covers computers

explanation.surface: Counting the computers kept in someone's lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Digits are the numerals nought to nine, single numbers.

clue.text: Changes one gradually at first within and, by chance, changes

indicators.note: within puts the pieces inside the word for changes

parts.note: varies means changes

indicators.note: at first means the first letter of the word

parts.note: a means one

explanation.surface: Things change gradually and then, by chance, change again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' places the pieces inside after the first two letters; 'Changes' opens the clue as wordplay and 'changes' closes it as definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Vagaries are unpredictable shifts, chance fluctuations of weather or fortune.

clue.text: Eager to see Camilla go glam

indicators.note: to see suggests the answer is visible within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Fans keen to watch Camilla dress up glamorously.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means keenly excited and impatient, eager to see what happens.

clue.text: How to supply team with fruity mix of tarts for winter season?

definitions.text: fruity mix of tarts for winter season?

parts.note: mincing the word meat chops it into new order, supplying team

explanation.surface: A recipe question about feeding a team on fruity Christmas tarts.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: mince (chop up) MEAT and you get TEAM. The winter season is Christmas, when mince pies are eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: This mix of dried fruit, suet and spice fills the small pies eaten at Christmas.
